title: PJM Load Forecast Report - January 2026 — Phase 65 Northern Virginia large-load delivery review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Northern Virginia large-load delivery reporting pack. PJM's 2026 forecast supplies the regional and zonal demand outlook used to frame Northern Virginia's grid-planning pressure while distinguishing near-term firm adjustments from more uncertain long-term projects.
key_findings: The report publishes a 2026 zonal load outlook and compares it with the prior forecast.
PJM distinguishes nearer-term firm large-load adjustments from longer-term non-firm projects.
A forecast remains a planning input rather than evidence that a named customer has interconnection, transmission, or service.
why_it_matters: Which records connect load forecasts, local land-use rules, utility decisions, transmission, environmental permits, water, service acceptance, and reliability? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. It refreshes the corridor demand baseline while making uncertainty treatment visible.
ftfn_relevance: Connects compute demand to regional planning evidence.
Supports a current forecast signal without turning demand into delivered capacity.
Creates a benchmark for later transmission and service records.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
Forecast demand is not a customer service commitment.
The report does not prove completed transmission, energization, or available spare capacity.
